audit.whatIsWrong: Stored chart read Quinn on four rows the packet and the mirror both give to Gnar or to Skill.
audit.why: Gnar shares Quinn's range: Boomerang Throw is 1100 and a caught return cuts its cooldown, so level 2 is his, and Mega Gnar's Wallop stun owns level 6. The mirror (gnar__quinn) already flipped these four rows as one atomic group.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2, 4 and 5 flipped together in both layers to Gnar/Skill/Gnar/Skill, with the two Gnar rows rated 3/10 (inverse of the mirror's 7/10) and the why text rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text had no numbers and treated GNAR! as a lane cooldown to trade around.
audit.why: GNAR! is 90s at rank 1 but gated behind the Rage bar, not the timer; Hop is 22s at rank 1 and Boomerang Throw 16s, and those are the cooldowns that actually open a step-up.
audit.corrected: Put the real Hop and Boomerang numbers into the rewritten strings and keyed the level-6 spike to the Rage bar.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five strings call Blinding Assault a blind on his autos; spikes[1] credits Vault with a knockback; nothing said his CC ends Behind Enemy Lines.
audit.why: Riot's Q text says Valor marks the enemy and hinders its vision — vision denial, not an attack blind, and it does nothing to Boomerang Throw or Hop, which are not attacks. Vault leaps Quinn away; it does not push Gnar. Behind Enemy Lines is a flagged channel, so Wallop's stun or a GNAR! knockup ends it.
audit.corrected: Replaced the blind framing with the nearsight, removed the knockback, and stated the channel interaction on the interactions line and the level-6 spike.

edits.before: Vault resets the spacing whenever he closes. Only take the trade when Gnar's GNAR! is down.
edits.after: Boomerang Throw out-ranges you at 1100 and a caught return refunds it before Vault is online.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Gnar must walk into your range.
edits.after: Full kit online: you win the Harrier-reset burst, he wins the boomerang-catch poke war. Rage timing decides it.

edits.before: Behind Enemy Lines exports your lead — roam on every shove. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Gnar's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Mega Gnar's Wallop stun pins you and cancels Behind Enemy Lines mid-channel; your R only roams, so the all-in is his.

edits.before: Youmuu's Ghostblade is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on GNAR!'s cooldown.
edits.after: Your Ghostblade spike and his Rage cycle cancel out — force only while his transform bar is empty.

edits.before: His biggest threat window: mega-Gnar's AoE stun pins you in place where your E knockback and W kite can't save you from his all-in.
edits.after: His biggest threat window: Mega Gnar's Wallop stun pins you and cancels Behind Enemy Lines — Vault repositions you, it will not save you.

edits.before: Track Gnar's GNAR! (Mega Stun): His Mega all-in. Vault it. When it is down — Vault-blind + R him.
edits.after: Wallop and GNAR! both cancel Behind Enemy Lines — channel only once spent. Hop is 22s at rank 1.

edits.before: Catch his boomerang miss, then E in and Q-blind to deny mini-Gnar's return-catch trade
edits.after: Step in on a missed boomerang, Vault for the Harrier auto, and hinder his vision with Q

edits.before: Gnar mirrors your range, so this isn't a free melee bully lane — his boomerang (Q) out-pokes you and a catch on the return doubles the damage, so don't walk forward while his bird is flying back to him. Your Q blind only neuters his autos, not his boomerang or hops, so it's worth less here than against juggernauts. Trade when his rage is low and his Q is mid-flight: E Vault in for the Harrier reset, get your blinded burst, then W out before he hops on you.
edits.after: Gnar mirrors your range, so this isn't a free melee bully lane — Boomerang Throw reaches 1100 and a catch on the return refunds its 16s, so don't walk forward while it is flying back to him. Blinding Assault only hinders his vision; it does nothing to the boomerang or to Hop, so it is worth less here than against juggernauts. Trade while his Rage is low and his Q is mid-flight: Vault in for the Harrier auto, then leave before he hops on you.

edits.before: By 2+ items you swing back ahead as a fed lethality marksman — mini-Gnar form is fragile and your Harrier burst plus Q blind on his autos out-duels him in an even-rage 1v1. But all game he carries one button that ruins you: mega-Gnar's stun into his team is instant death for your no-front-to-back frame. Win the side lanes with your roam, never facecheck him at full rage, and only duel when his transform is on cooldown.
edits.after: By 2+ items you swing back ahead as a fed lethality marksman — mini Gnar is fragile and your Harrier burst out-duels him in an even-Rage 1v1. But all game he carries one button that ruins you: a Wallop stun into his team is instant death for your no-front-to-back frame, and it ends Behind Enemy Lines on the spot. Win side lanes with your roam and never facecheck him at full Rage.

notes: The mirror's leftover sweep items apply here too: dosFull[2].t 'E-vault out of his Mega all-in' and the breakdown.cooldowns / breakdown.trading template strings still carry the 'Q-blind' framing, but those templates have no room inside the length band for the correction. Flagging rather than forcing them. GNAR! is Rage-gated, so several inherited strings that speak of 'GNAR!'s cooldown' are conceptually wrong even where I could not rewrite them.
